narrative.overview:
HOI4 uses dark blue water, muted country colors, strong terrain relief, thin borders, and outlined Barlow names. EU4 uses brighter political colors, pale coastal water, fine borders, subtle relief, and spaced Cinzel names. These are original AltBorder styles informed by the two games. HOI4 is the default theme.

The editor uses dark surfaces, warm gold actions, sans-serif headings, and compact controls. Country tools float over the desktop map and form a collapsible bottom sheet on phones. Flat mode tabs and a fixed action footer keep the active task clear. The map combines SVG geometry with projected raster layers. A theme changes the map appearance. Country ownership, geometry, names, and explicit colors stay intact.
keyCharacteristics: Two distinct map palettes with thin country borders.
Strong HOI4 relief and subtle EU4 relief over live country fills.
Uppercase Barlow or Cinzel country names without map flags.
Dark country tools with warm gold actions and a two-choice map theme control.
A full-width map, a floating country panel, and a phone bottom sheet with visible primary actions.

rules.name: The Map Scope Rule
rules.body: Apply theme colors and map label styles to the map. Keep the dark and gold editor palette. The wordmark shares the self-hosted Barlow family; editor controls retain their sans-serif stack.

rules.name: The Scenario Color Rule
rules.body: Derive default display colors from the selected theme and the canonical base map. Preserve custom countries and explicit entity colors, including an explicit choice equal to the stored base color. Raster shading may change their visible tone without changing their stored fill color.

rules.name: The HUD Type Rule
rules.body: Use sans-serif headings in country tools. Keep the self-hosted Barlow wordmark separate from the map's outlined country labels.

rules.name: The Map Name Rule
rules.body: Use the selected theme's uppercase country names on the map. Keep flags in the editor.

rules.name: The Visible Action Rule
rules.body: Keep Transfer and ready Divide actions outside the scrollable tool body. Preserve country context and mode access when the phone sheet is closed.

rules.name: The Live Land Rule
rules.body: Align raster layers to the active map projection and clip land textures to the current country paths. Theme layers must not take pointer input. Preserve asset provenance in `public/map-themes/SOURCES.md` and the supplied font licenses.

dos: Do use the selected theme for default country display colors.
Do keep the six-color canonical baseline for state and shared-link compatibility.
Do keep country borders thin: HOI4 (0.95px) and EU4 (0.8px).
Do preserve explicit country color values when themes change or scenarios load.
Do show more region detail as the user zooms in.
Do keep ocean labels at full opacity where they are visible.
Do keep selection feedback, keyboard focus, and reduced-motion behavior.
Do keep Transfer and ready Divide actions visible while tool settings scroll.
Do retain country context and all four mode tabs in the closed phone sheet.
Do keep the map full height beside a floating panel on portrait tablets.
Do give a focused phone form the available height while the software keyboard is open.
Do keep touch controls at least 44px and text inputs at 16px.
Do keep the landscape form and its action in the visible viewport while the software keyboard is open.
donts: Don't apply map colors or outlined country-label styles to editor controls.
Don't add flags to country names on the map.
Don't use the default palette to replace explicit scenario colors.
Don't bake political colors into the terrain rasters.
Don't replace live map geometry or input targets with raster artwork.
